# Sasha Greenspan, PhD

352-575-8605 | sasha.greenspan@gmail.com | LinkedIn | Google Scholar | Baltimore, MD

## SUMMARY
Research operations leader with 20+ years building and scaling complex clinical and biological research programs. Deep experience leading end-to-end, device-enabled clinical studies (start-up through close-out), coordinating sites and vendors, and overseeing GCP/ICH-compliant workflows. Known for translating regulatory and technical complexity into efficient, patient-centered execution that drives enrollment, retention, and data quality.

## CLINICAL RESEARCH EXPERIENCE

### Supervisory Research Administrative Coordinator (2022–2025)
*Clinical Project Manager-equivalent | Regulatory Specialist-equivalent*
**Pediatric Neuroimaging Core, Marcus Autism Center, School of Medicine, Emory University** — Atlanta, GA

- Led end-to-end operations for multimillion-dollar, device-enabled clinical studies, serving as primary operational and regulatory owner across sites, vendors, data, and study teams
- Study lifecycle management: Built REDCap databases; prepared regulatory start-up packages; activated new research sites; coordinated vendors for imaging hardware, wearables, and data systems; managed timelines, budgets, and milestones; conducted monthly data audits; coordinated cross-functional teams; proactively mitigated operational and regulatory risks; Led regulatory close-out, data reconciliation, and reporting
- Regulatory leadership: Led IRB submissions, amendments, and continuing reviews; maintained regulatory binders; interpreted and applied regulatory codes to ensure ICH-GCP and FDA compliance
- Team leadership: Onboarded study staff; designed and delivered GCP/ICH and protocol training; authored SOPs, study manuals, and scripts to standardize site practices; supported staff performance and retention
- Impact: Tripled enrollment for hard-to-reach populations and achieved the highest participation of historically underrepresented groups in the program's history

## ADDITIONAL OPERATIONS & PROGRAM LEADERSHIP

### Program Administrator (2024–present)
**Dr. James A. Ferguson EID RISE Graduate Research Fellowship**
*Center for Excellence in Public Health Leadership, Kennedy Krieger Institute* — Baltimore, MD
*Joint faculty appointment: Assistant Scientist, Dept of Molecular Microbiology and Immunology, Bloomberg School of Public Health, Johns Hopkins University*

- Lead strategic planning, recruitment, training, and engagement (100+ annual events) for nationwide public health workforce pipeline supporting 40+ graduate infectious disease research fellows annually

### Operations Lead & Co-founder (2019–2025)
**Student Network for Amphibian Pathogen Surveillance (SNAPS)** — Remote

- Scaled network from 0 to 1,250+ student participants across 50+ institutions in 33 states
- Built data collection, communication, and training infrastructure for distributed research execution

### Research Associate | Postdoctoral Scientist (2018–2022)
**Becker Lab, Department of Biological Sciences, University of Alabama** — Tuscaloosa, AL

- Led international, multi-site emerging infectious disease field research program and molecular analysis pipeline
- Managed buildout of two molecular labs (budgets, vendor contracts, procurement, training, compliance)
- Co-managed $1M+ in federal funding; developed budgets, wrote grants (2 NSF awards), and forecasted spend
- Mentored and facilitated research & publication output of 8 graduate students; authored 17 papers

### Research Ecologist (2005–2014)
**UGA Marine Institute | Jones Center at Ichauway | La Selva Biological Station | National Park Service** — Various locations

- Implemented multi-site global change research, wildlife infectious disease surveillance, and conservation efforts

## EDUCATION
- **PhD cum laude**, Biology, James Cook University (2014–2018)
- **MS**, Biology, University of Maine (2010–2011)
- **BA**, Environmental Science & Anthropology, Wesleyan University (2002–2006)
